source.title: GNU Bash man page: Parameter Expansion (substring expansion)
GNU Bash man page: Compound Commands (while and until)
GNU Bash man page: REDIRECTION ({varname} descriptor allocation)

rewrite.reason: Weak card (strawman false side), rewritten rather than dropped: dropping sr3-02, sr3-06, sr3-07 and sr3-09 would leave r3 with 8 cards. This uses the verifier's replacement on the documented :- versus negative-offset trap. Confirmed on man7 Parameter Expansion: 'a negative offset must be separated from the colon by at least one space to avoid being confused with the :- expansion'. Bash 5.3.20 gives [abcdef] for ${x:-2} and [ef] for ${x: -2}.
rewrite.statement: With x=abcdef, Bash expands ${x:-2} to ef, the last two characters of x.
rewrite.explanation: Written as ${x:-2}, this is the :- default-value operator; x is set and non-null, so the result is abcdef. A negative substring offset must be separated from the colon by a space, as in ${x: -2}.
rewrite.misconception: ${x:-2} is a negative substring offset that counts from the end of the value.
rewrite.sourceTitle: GNU Bash man page: Parameter Expansion

rewrite.reason: Duplicate of sr9-08 (list status is the last command's status), rewritten rather than dropped: dropping sr7-04, sr7-05 and sr7-10 would leave r7 at 3 true / 6 false. This uses the verifier's replacement, with the 'because its body never runs' clause removed (a negation and an answer-giving reason). Confirmed on man7 Compound Commands: 'The exit status of the while and until commands is the exit status of the last command executed in list-2, or zero if none was executed.' Bash 5.3.20 prints while=0.
rewrite.statement: Bash gives while false; do :; done an exit status of zero.
rewrite.explanation: A while or until loop returns the status of the last body command it ran, or zero when the body never ran, so the failed condition's status is discarded.
rewrite.sourceTitle: GNU Bash man page: Compound Commands (while and until)

rewrite.reason: Duplicate across decks (linux-command-line-sr7-03, 2>&1 before >), rewritten rather than dropped: dropping the four duplicates would leave r12 with 8 cards at 3 true / 5 false. This uses the verifier's {varname} replacement. Confirmed on man7 REDIRECTION: 'the shell allocates a file descriptor greater than or equal to 10 and assigns it to varname'. Bash 5.3.20 gives fd=10.
rewrite.statement: For exec {fd}>log, Bash assigns fd a descriptor number of 10 or higher.
rewrite.explanation: A {varname} word in place of a descriptor number makes Bash allocate a descriptor of at least 10 and store its number in the variable, so scripts avoid hard-coded numbers.

rewrite.reason: Source problem: man7 bash(1) does not say that a redirection on a compound command covers the commands inside it. The Bash Reference Manual's Compound Commands section does: 'Any redirections associated with a compound command apply to all commands within that compound command unless explicitly overridden.' gnu.org refused connections today, so I confirmed this sentence in the released Bash 5.3 bash.info shipped with 5.3.20. Statement and explanation are unchanged.
rewrite.statement: Bash applies { printf a; printf b; } >out to both printf commands.
rewrite.explanation: A redirection attached to the brace group applies to its command list. Both printf commands write through the redirected stdout.

rewrite.reason: tell: in r10, 'exits before printf x' appeared only on true cards (scan tell 1). The fact (errexit ignores a pipeline inverted with !) and the answer (false) are unchanged. Bash 5.3.20 prints x.
rewrite.statement: With set -e, Bash exits before printf x in ! true; printf x.
rewrite.explanation: Bash ignores errexit for a pipeline whose status is inverted with !. This script therefore continues to printf x.
rewrite.misconception: A negated pipeline's failed overall status triggers errexit.
rewrite.sourceTitle: GNU Bash man page: set builtin: errexit

rewrite.reason: tell: this moves a second false card into the 'exits before printf x' frame, which balances scan tell 1. The fact (errexit is ignored throughout a function called as an if condition) and the answer (false) are unchanged. Bash 5.3.20 prints x.
rewrite.statement: With set -e, Bash exits before printf x in f(){ false; printf x; }; if f; then :; fi.
rewrite.explanation: Calling f as an if condition makes Bash ignore errexit throughout that function body. The false is followed by printf x.
rewrite.misconception: A tested function call retains errexit handling for failures inside its body.
rewrite.sourceTitle: GNU Bash man page: set builtin: errexit

rewrite.reason: tell: as an ordering word, 'before' was 1 true to 6 false across the deck (scan tell 2). This rewords the true card's ordering claim to use 'before'. The fact (word splitting comes before pathname expansion) and the answer (true) are unchanged.
rewrite.statement: With x='*.cfg', Bash splits unquoted $x before applying pathname expansion to its words.
rewrite.explanation: An unquoted expansion can supply a glob pattern for the later pathname-expansion stage.

rewrite.reason: tell: the 'With X off' option premise was 1 true to 5 false (scan tell 3). This removes the premise from one false card. The fact (local - restores only set options, not shopt) and the answer (false) are unchanged. Bash 5.3.20 shows nullglob on after f.
rewrite.statement: For f(){ local -; shopt -s nullglob; }, Bash returns nullglob to its earlier off state when f ends.
rewrite.explanation: local - restores options changed through set. This shopt change persists, so nullglob remains enabled after f returns.
rewrite.misconception: local - restores shopt settings together with set options.
rewrite.sourceTitle: GNU Bash man page: local builtin

edits.notes:
Verification: man7 bash(1) returned HTTP 200 (GNU Bash 5.3; man7's HTML rendering is dated 2026-09-09). www.gnu.org refused connections (ECONNREFUSED) through both curl and WebFetch today, as the prompt warns. For GNU reference-manual wording I used the released Bash 5.3 bash.info shipped with Homebrew GNU bash 5.3.20 (5.3 plus patch 020, the pinned set). I ran every rewritten statement in bash 5.3.20: ${x:-2} gives abcdef; while false loop gives 0; exec {fd} gives 10; '! true; printf x' prints x under set -e; a tested f prints x; nullglob is on after local - and shopt; pipefail plus -e exits 1.

Judgment calls:
(1) sr8-06 and sr9-08 duplicate each other. Both verifiers flagged one against the other; the scan chose to drop sr9-08. I dropped only sr9-08 and kept sr8-06, because the prompt places last-command function status in r8 and dropping both would remove the fact entirely.
(2) sr3-02 is dropped, not re-sourced. The verifier's POSIX URL is outside the prompt's allowed sources (gnu.org and man7.org). Neither man7 nor the released bash.info states that an unneeded word stays unexpanded; bash.info says only 'WORD is subject to tilde expansion, ...'. Because of this drop I rewrote sr3-07 instead of dropping it, to keep r3 at 9.
(3) r7 and r12 each needed one rewrite to stay within the floor and the split. I picked sr7-05 (the while/until zero-status fact; the nocasematch replacement for sr7-10 is a name giveaway) and sr12-01 (the {varname} fact). I rejected the here-string tilde replacement because a verifier saw unquoted ~ ignore a HOME reassigned inside a 5.3.20 -c script.
(4) The sr12-04 source fix points to the GNU Compound Commands page, which I could not open live. Its sentence is confirmed in the released 5.3 bash.info. Re-open the URL once gnu.org is reachable.

Tell work used 4 of the 5 allowed rewords: sr10-04 and sr10-05 (the 'exits before printf x' frame is now 3 true / 2 false, counting sr10-08's 'stops before'); sr2-01 (adds a true 'before'); sr8-12 (removes a false option-off premise; after sr11-11 is dropped, option-off premises are 3 false / 1 true). Dropping sr3-02 brings the 'Bash runs X before Y' false template down to the cap of two (sr7-06, sr11-05).

Remaining weaker signals I did not change: 'one argument/operand' is 3/0 true (sr1-03, sr1-05, sr6-03), and sr4-02 still uses 'requires' on a false card. The deck overall is now 63 true / 77 false; every section is within the rule, but a later pass could add true cards in r1, r3, r4, r7, r9, r11 and r12.

Coverage lost through drops: r11 no longer has a cleanup-status-preservation card (sr11-01), r9 no longer tests explicit exit status, and r12 now has 4 descriptor cards and 4 here-document/here-string cards instead of about six each. Candidate replacements already checked by the verifiers, if a top-up round runs later: r11 trap 'cleanup; exit $?' clobbering status; r11 signals ignored on entry cannot be trapped; r12 3<<END; r12 noclobber and /dev/null; r9 bare exit after false; r9 128+N for SIGTERM.

cards.explanation: A {varname} word in place of a descriptor number makes Bash allocate a descriptor of at least 10 and store its number in the variable, so scripts avoid hard-coded numbers.

cards.explanation: A redirection attached to a compound command such as a brace group applies to every command inside it unless one overrides it, so both printf outputs go to out.
cards.reason: I applied the wording lens fix: the statement now names the redirection as the thing applied, and the explanation now says compound command, to match the source. The fact is unchanged and the fact lens agrees with it. gnu.org timed out again today, but the same sentence is in the released Bash 5.3.20 bash.info (lines 800-802): 'redirections associated with a compound command apply to all commands within that compound command unless explicitly overridden.' Statement 90 chars, explanation 160.

cards.explanation: Bash ignores errexit for a pipeline whose status is inverted with !. This script therefore continues to printf x.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep it. I confirmed the fact on man7 set -e today: the shell does not exit 'if the command's return value is being inverted with !'. The 'exits before printf x' frame now has 3 true and 2 false cards. That is the most the false-template rule allows.

cards.reason: Both lenses keep it. I confirmed the fact on man7 set -e today: when a shell function runs in a context where -e is ignored, 'none of the commands executed within the compound command or function body will be affected by the -e setting'. This is the second and last false card allowed in the frame.

cards.statement: With x='a *.cfg', Bash splits unquoted $x into two words before applying pathname expansion to them.
cards.explanation: Word splitting comes before pathname expansion, so the unquoted value first becomes the words a and *.cfg, and Bash then matches *.cfg against filenames.
cards.reason: I merged the fixes: the wording lens's fix matches the improvement the fact lens marked as optional. With x='*.cfg' word splitting changes nothing, so the order could not be seen. The fact, the answer and the 'before' wording used for tell balance all stay. I confirmed the order on man7 EXPANSION today ('word splitting; pathname expansion; and quote removal') and in Pathname Expansion ('After word splitting ... bash scans each word'). Statement 100 chars, explanation 153.

cards.statement: For f(){ local -; shopt -s nullglob; }, Bash returns nullglob to its earlier off state when f ends.
cards.explanation: local - restores options changed through set. This shopt change persists, so nullglob remains enabled after f returns.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep it. I confirmed the fact on man7 local today: local - restores 'any shell options changed using the set builtin'. nullglob is a shopt option. The deck's assumed context already gives nullglob as off at the start.
